newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades ease as refinery covering fades.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades ease as refinery covering fades.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices eased back early Wednesday, both on an outright and differential basis, as the refinery covering seen the previous day faded, traders said.

Benchmark July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was down around 30 cents at $18.90 a barrel in NYMEX trading mid-morning, while cash WTI/Cushing was about eight to 10 cents above that factoring in the Exchange for Physical (EFP) premium.

The generally bearish tone to outright prices was set by the latest American Petroleume Institute and Department of Energy weekly reports showing the trend of crude stocks increases and high products output continuing.
Also, differentials for he major traded grades declined by between five and 15 cents, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire the biggest loser and the only grade to trade early, traders said.
HLS traded at a 40 cents discount to WTI during the morning, down from deals on Tuesday at 22 cents and 28 cents and back in line with Monday's level.

Among other grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was down five cents at a five/10 cents discount, West Texas Sour/Midland was quoted 10 cents weaker at $1.35 and Eugene Island was down five cents at around $1.80 under.
"There was some short-covering by refiners who waited to cover their requirements but found there were no unsold cargoes out there," said a trader for a large commodity trading house.
The closed "arbitrage" to sell North Sea barrels into the U.S. Gulf had helped firm up differentials, though the "there was not tremendous volume," said a Houston broker.

Traders also noted that the market was muted by the absence of many players who attended BP America's annual baseball game in Cleveland on Tuesday and were still there for the company's golf outing on Wednesday.
